newsitem.title: JAPAN: Korean banks in Tokyo face higher funding costs.
newsitem.headline: Korean banks in Tokyo face higher funding costs.

text.p: Japanese branches of South Korean banks are facing extra costs for raising funds in the Tokyo money market after the recent collapse of Hanbo Steel Co, market sources said on Tuesday.
Korean banks are paying a premium of about 10 basis points over the prevailing unsecured overnight call rate of around 0.50 percent, the sources said.

However, the Korean banks' funding difficulties are having little impact on Japan's interbank money market rates, money traders said. "As the Bank of Korea (BOK) is providing liquidity, we are not concerned about fund-raising," said an official at a Korean bank's Tokyo branch.
Some Korean banks in Tokyo are raising needed funds through remittances from their Seoul headquarters, Japanese money traders said.
The so-called "Korea premium" surfaced on Friday, as Japanese banks reduced credit to Korean banks on concerns that the Hanbo collapse could inflict serious damage on Korean banks' creditworthiness.
Hanbo Steel, South Korea's second largest steel maker, defaulted on debt repayments last month after piling up some five trillion won in loans.
